card.title: When I Believed in the Rules
card.instruction: Perform the version of yourself who once trusted the institution, tradition, or process. Use its old language even as your confidence slips.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to the complaint desk. We used to promise 'a person, not a number.' I still have my badge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need my refund today. There's only a ticket machine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take a number. Someone will call it. Someone always did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ticket says to post it away and wait six weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll write 'a person, not a number' on the envelope. They may still recognise it.

mechanism: A revives the old service promise and badge, then keeps using that language as the current complaint process erodes confidence.
confusable: Unlike defending current procedure as correct, A performs the earlier trusting institutional self while visibly recognizing that the process has changed.
comparison: The complaint alternative carries an old slogan onto a delayed postal request; the club alternative seeks the crest while losing an established locker.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
